# Security & Access Control Checklist: User Login

**Purpose**: Pre-implementation reviewer gate on the quality of the security/access-control
requirements for the User Login feature (authentication boundary, redirect logic, session
handling) before `/speckit-tasks` and `/speckit-implement` begin.
**Created**: 2026-09-04
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md) ([plan.md](../plan.md), [research.md](../research.md), [contracts/sign-in-route.md](../contracts/sign-in-route.md))

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 Are requirements defined for what should happen if the Clerk instance is misconfigured (e.g., the required sign-in strategy disabled) at deploy time, beyond the operational note in research.md? [Gap, research.md #3]
- [ ] CHK002 Are requirements specified for how a missing or unset sign-in redirect configuration should be detected or defaulted, rather than only documented as a setup step? [Gap, research.md #1]
- [ ] CHK003 Are requirements defined for session-expiry behavior beyond "treat as unauthenticated on the next request" — e.g., whether the user sees any in-page notice versus a silent redirect? [Gap, Spec §Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK004 Is there a requirement covering the maximum acceptable time to display a failed-login error, distinct from the success-path timing target? [Gap, Spec §SC-001]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK005 Is "appropriate error" (FR-006) clarified enough to know whether distinct messages are required for wrong-password versus unknown-account cases, or whether a single generic message satisfies it? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006]
- [ ] CHK006 Is "protected application page" (FR-004) defined precisely enough that a reviewer can determine, from the spec alone, which routes are in scope versus explicitly public? [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK007 Is the "clear error state" required when the authentication provider is unreachable (Edge Cases) distinguished clearly enough from the invalid-credentials error state (FR-006) that they won't be implemented identically by mistake? [Clarity, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK008 Are the always-`/dashboard` redirect requirements (FR-003, FR-005) stated clearly enough to prevent a future reader from assuming the existing role-aware route-access function should be reused for this page? [Consistency, research.md #2]
- [ ] CHK009 Do the sign-in page's access requirements align with the three existing `redirectToSignIn()` call sites' behavior, with no visitor state left uncovered by either document? [Consistency, contracts/sign-in-route.md]

## Acceptance Criteria Quality

- [ ] CHK010 Can SC-002 ("100% of attempts... result in redirection... no protected content ever rendered") be verified in a way that is objective and observable, rather than relying on implementation inspection? [Measurability, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK011 Does SC-003 ("sign-in form never shown to a signed-in user") account for a session that becomes invalid mid-request, or only the straightforward already-signed-in case? [Measurability, Spec §SC-003]

## Scenario Coverage

- [ ] CHK012 Are requirements defined for a signed-in user whose session is invalidated concurrently with a request to `/sign-in` (race between redirect decision and session state)? [Coverage, Gap]
- [ ] CHK013 Are requirements defined for a signed-in user whose role/metadata is missing or unrecognized specifically in the context of the sign-in page's own redirect decision (as opposed to the dashboard's role check)? [Coverage, Spec §FR-003, Spec §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK014 Are the account-recovery and identity-verification requirements (Edge Cases) specific enough to know what "surfaced within or linked from the sign-in experience" implies for this page, or is that left fully open? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Edge Case Coverage

- [ ] CHK015 Is there a requirement addressing repeated/rapid failed sign-in attempts from the application's perspective, even though enforcement is delegated to Clerk? [Edge Case, Gap]
- [ ] CHK016 Is the "authentication provider unreachable" edge case scoped only to initial page load, or does it also need to cover an outage occurring mid-submission after the user has entered credentials? [Edge Case, Spec §Edge Cases]

## Non-Functional Requirements (Security)

- [ ] CHK017 Are requirements specified for keeping server-only secrets (e.g., the Clerk secret key) separated from public configuration (e.g., the sign-in redirect URL), beyond the general constitution principle? [Gap, plan.md Constitution Check Principle 9]
- [ ] CHK018 Is there an explicit requirement that the sign-in page must never receive or render protected data, independent of SC-002's redirect-behavior framing? [Gap, Spec §SC-002]
- [ ] CHK019 Is "defense in depth" (independent authentication checks at more than one layer) stated as a requirement anywhere in spec.md, or does it exist only as an implementation choice in plan.md/research.md? [Ambiguity, plan.md Project Structure]

## Dependencies & Assumptions

- [ ] CHK020 Does the assumption that "registered users already have valid Clerk accounts" (Spec §Assumptions) leave a gap in how a user without an account is expected to learn they cannot sign in? [Assumption, Spec §Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK021 Is the dependency on the Clerk instance being configured with the correct sign-in strategy (research.md #3) reflected in the spec's own Assumptions section, or only in planning artifacts? [Traceability, Spec §Assumptions, research.md #3]

## Ambiguities & Conflicts

- [ ] CHK022 Does excluding "role-based authorization" (FR-012) create ambiguity about whether role is read at all during sign-in, versus simply not used to branch the redirect? [Ambiguity, Spec §FR-012, research.md #2]

## Notes

- Mark items `[x]` only after review confirms the requirement-quality criterion is satisfied
- Leave items unchecked when they still require clarification, correction, or reviewer evaluation
- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist checkbox state as a gate and must not modify markers
- `checklists/requirements.md` has a separate built-in lifecycle maintained by `/speckit-specify` and `/speckit-clarify`
- Add comments or findings inline
- Link to relevant resources or documentation
- Items are numbered sequentially for easy reference
